advice: Test one 32-column B panel at a time, packed inside gemm as packed_b[k*32+c] = B[k*512+c] for k=0..511 and c=0..31. Allocate 64 KiB once, pack each panel before use, and change the full512 tile traversal to process that panel across all eight 64-row blocks before packing the next. Keep the existing A packing, two K loops, FP32 FMOPA order, stores, and one SME entry/exit. For each panel, advance the original B source by 128 bytes; after its eight row blocks, rewind A and C by 1,048,576 bytes and advance C and the source B panel by 128 bytes. For packed B, advance 128 bytes per K step, rewind 65,536 bytes after each tile, and start the next packed panel at the same buffer base. This tests whether contiguous B-panel reuse across rows offsets panel packing and the added allocation; no gain is established. Keep the n!=512 fallback and n<=0 behavior unchanged. Check all pointer and stride equations, panel boundaries, full output coverage and overwrite, allocation-failure fallback, general sizes and tails, and tolerance 0.002. Measure packing, allocation and cleanup within gemm using fresh paired controls under the unchanged power mode and settings.
risks: This changes the B layout and traversal together, so any outcome applies to the complete change and cannot isolate reuse from packing or traversal effects. It adds 64 KiB allocation and copies 1 MiB of B data per call. Correctness depends on resetting packed-B and A/C pointers at each tile and covering every row and column exactly once. Performance is unverified; historical scores are noisy and do not establish causality.
